results.title: Uncovering wind power forecasting uncertainty sources and their propagation through the whole modelling chain - ScienceDirect
results.content: # Uncovering wind power forecasting uncertainty sources and their propagation through the whole modelling chain☆. Main source of uncertainty through modelling chain of wind power forecast is defined. First, the definition of uncertainty sources throughout the forecast modelling chain acts as a guiding line for checking and evaluating the uncertainty of a wind power forecast system/model. For each of the types of uncertainty sources, uncertainty mitigation strategies are provided, starting from the planning phase of wind farms, the establishment of a forecasting system through the operational phase and market phase. Highlights are a qualitative review and discussion including: (1) forecasting uncertainty exists and propagates everywhere throughout the entire modelling chain, from the planning phase to the market phase; (2) the mitigation efforts should be exerted in every modelling step; (3) standardised uncertainty validation practice, including why global data samples are required for forecasters to improve model performance and for forecast users to select and evaluate forecast model outputs.

results.title: Current and future state of evaluation of large language models for medical summarization tasks | npj Health Systems
results.content: # Current and future state of evaluation of large language models for medical summarization tasks. Large Language Models have expanded the potential for clinical Natural Language Generation (NLG), presenting new opportunities to manage the vast amounts of medical text. In this review, we investigated the current landscape of evaluation metrics for NLG in healthcare and proposed a future direction to address the resource constraints of expert human evaluation while balancing alignment with human judgments. ### Human evaluation of large language models in healthcare: gaps, challenges, and the need for standardization. The rapid development of Large Language Models (LLMs) has led to significant advancements in the field of Natural Language Generation (NLG).
